prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a polished 12-portrait emotion exploration sheet for Drain Damage EASY MODE using the supplied reference board. User selected design #1: ruffled bonnet tied in a bow under chin, pacifier in mouth, chubby shirtless chest-up adult baby caricature. Apply this identical costume theme to BOTH heroes: Tony exactly like reference #1 in blue; Sean like reference #4 in orange/yellow, with his bald head and salt-and-pepper goatee visible. Preserve their adult facial identities and chubby cheeks/shoulders. Match reference's detailed painted cartoon game style, crisp outlines, warm shading.
Layout: landscape sheet with TWO clearly labeled rows, SIX equal-sized bust portraits per row. Top TONY, bottom SEAN. Consistent size, chest-up crop and costume in every cell. Same six emotions in columns for both heroes: JOY, FURY, PANIC, SADNESS, SURPRISE, SMUG. Keep the pacifier naturally in the mouth in EVERY portrait, including laughing and surprise; convey emotions through expressive eyes, eyebrows, cheeks and head tilt, not by removing pacifier. Joy squinting delighted eyes; fury deeply furrowed brows; panic wide frightened eyes and tense eyebrows; sadness watery eyes and one tear; surprise round eyes and high eyebrows; smug half-lidded sideways glance and raised eyebrow. Exaggerate distinctly enough to read as small game portraits while retaining familiar faces. Tony signature spiky black hair prominently peeks from frilled blue bonnet; Sean bald crown partly visible inside frilled orange bonnet and full short chin goatee below orange pacifier. Bare chubby shoulders and upper chest only. No hats changing between emotions, no bibs, no sleep caps, no extra props, no lower-body framing. Pale warm-gray paper backdrop, thin navy dividers, header "EASY MODE — EMOTION STUDY". Clear column labels exactly JOY, FURY, PANIC, SADNESS, SURPRISE, SMUG; row labels TONY and SEAN. These are concept alternatives for user selection, not gameplay screenshots. High-resolution wide composition with generous room for all twelve portraits, no clipped faces or bonnet edges.
